short: Raising online menu prices to absorb commission and packaging.
seoTitle: Menu Price Padding — Meaning, Formula and Example
metaDescription: Raising online menu prices to absorb commission and packaging. Without padding, every online order earns materially less than the same dish sold in-house.
definition: Menu price padding is setting higher prices on delivery platforms than in the restaurant, so that commission, packaging and funded discounts still leave the intended margin.
bodyHtml:
Why Menu Price Padding matters

Without padding, every online order earns materially less than the same dish sold in-house. With too much padding, listings look expensive next to competitors and conversion falls.

Menu Price Padding formula

Online price = Target net price ÷ (1 − commission rate)

Add packaging cost before applying the divisor.

How Menu Price Padding works in practice

Work backwards from the net realisation you need after commission and packaging, then sanity-check the result against comparable listings nearby. Pad by category rather than uniformly, since low-value items suffer most.

Worked example

To net ₹300 at a 22% commission, the listed price needs to be about ₹385 before packaging.

faq.question: Is it legal to charge more online?
faq.answer: Menu pricing is commercial, though platform agreements may include parity terms — read yours before setting prices.

faq.question: How much padding is too much?
faq.answer: When your listing stops converting against comparable restaurants nearby, which shows up quickly in order volume.
